boundary_condition: Do not rank United above other preferred carriers solely from this habit; the evidence only establishes repeated inclusion in multi-carrier sets.
canonical_value: Include United as a soft preferred carrier option when it is otherwise suitable and comparable.
condition: When searching for commercial flights and no current-trip instruction specifies a different carrier set.
default_action: Include United among the preferred carrier options when it is otherwise suitable and comparable.
exception_condition: Use other carriers when United is unavailable, unsuitable for the itinerary, materially worse, or excluded by a current-trip instruction.
name: united_soft_carrier_option
preference_value: United is a recurring acceptable carrier to include among preferred flight options, but is not required or uniquely favored.
rationale: Repeated evidence across distinct trips supports United as a recurring acceptable option within multi-carrier preference sets, while consistently preserving flexibility to choose other suitable carriers.

boundary_condition: This is a soft preference: the evidence supports Delta as a favored option, not as the only acceptable airline or an always-first choice over every other preferred carrier.
canonical_value: Include and softly favor Delta among suitable flight options without treating it as exclusive.
condition: When choosing among flight carriers and Delta is available while also satisfying the trip's schedule, route, price, and stop constraints.
default_action: Search for or present Delta options as part of the preferred carrier set, and favor Delta when it is otherwise comparable to alternatives.
exception_condition: Use another acceptable carrier when Delta is unavailable, materially worse, or does not meet the current trip constraints.
name: Delta as a soft preferred carrier option
preference_value: Delta is a preferred airline to include in the flight shortlist, but not an exclusive carrier requirement.
rationale: Repeated evidence across distinct trips supports Delta as a soft preferred carrier, including one explicit direct preference, without establishing exclusivity or overriding itinerary constraints.

boundary_condition: Treat this as a soft default; departures close to afternoon may be considered when true afternoon options are limited or unattractive.
canonical_value: Prefer afternoon departures for the return leg, considering departures close to afternoon when needed.
condition: When booking or comparing round-trip flights and selecting the return leg departure time.
default_action: Present return-flight options departing in the afternoon first and let the user choose among them.
exception_condition: Do not generalize this return-leg preference to outbound legs, and follow any explicit timing requirement for the current trip.
name: afternoon_return_departure_preference
preference_value: Prefer the return flight to depart in the afternoon.
rationale: Keep the calibrated representative as a distinct return-leg preference. Its leg-specific scope is not semantically interchangeable with the general afternoon-departure policy, and the evidence supports only a soft afternoon default with nearby times as a fallback.

boundary_condition: Apply only as a general time-of-day preference without inferring a route, date, or leg-specific requirement.
canonical_value: Prefer morning flight departures when no trip-specific timing constraint applies.
condition: When choosing a flight departure time and no trip-specific timing constraint overrides the preference.
default_action: Present morning departure options first.
exception_condition: Follow an explicitly stated timing requirement for the current trip; no reusable fallback is established when morning options are unavailable.
name: prefer_morning_flight_departures
preference_value: Prefer morning flight departures.
rationale: Keep the calibrated representative as a reusable general preference. Morning and afternoon are contrasting alternatives rather than aliases, and current-trip timing requirements continue to override this soft default.

boundary_condition: Do not apply the preference to a leg for which another time of day is explicitly requested.
canonical_value: Prefer afternoon flight departures when workable options are available.
condition: When selecting a flight departure time and afternoon options are available.
default_action: Prioritize departure options in the afternoon.
exception_condition: Use another departure period when explicitly requested or when no workable afternoon option is available.
name: prefer_afternoon_flight_departures
preference_value: Prefer afternoon flight departures.
rationale: Keep the calibrated representative as the general afternoon alternative. It must remain separate from the morning preference and from the return-leg-specific afternoon policy because those policies differ in value or scope.

boundary_condition: Treat this as a preference rather than an absolute requirement unless the user explicitly says no layovers for the current trip.
canonical_value: Prefer nonstop flights, with a one-stop itinerary as a conditional fallback.
condition: When searching for outbound or return flights, prioritize nonstop options.
default_action: Search for and present a nonstop itinerary first.
exception_condition: If no suitable nonstop flight is available, a one-stop option may be acceptable, but confirm the tradeoff before booking.
name: Prefer nonstop flights
preference_value: Nonstop flights are generally preferred.
rationale: The frozen representative is supported by repeated requests for nonstop travel. The evidence also supports treating nonstop as a preference rather than an unconditional rule because one example explicitly allows at most one stop.

boundary_condition: Do not let price override explicit requirements such as Wi-Fi, acceptable layover length, nonstop service when requested, or required departure and return timing.
canonical_value: Choose the cheapest flight that satisfies all stated must-have itinerary and amenity constraints.
condition: When comparing flights that meet the trip's required timing, connectivity, and onboard-feature needs.
default_action: Rank acceptable options by price and choose the cheapest one.
exception_condition: Choose a more expensive option when the cheapest violates a stated must-have or has an unacceptably long or inconvenient layover.
name: Cheapest acceptable flight
preference_value: Prefer the lowest-priced flight that still satisfies essential itinerary and amenity constraints.
rationale: Repeated examples support a stable price-first policy among flights that satisfy explicit itinerary and amenity requirements; the frozen representative remains unchanged.

boundary_condition: Treat the preference as a flexible later-day window ranging from afternoon to after 6:00 p.m., not as a fixed cutoff
canonical_value: Prefer afternoon or evening return departures when workable
condition: When selecting a return flight and multiple departure times are available
default_action: Prioritize return options departing in the afternoon or evening
exception_condition: Use another departure period when the traveler explicitly requests it for the current trip or no later-day option is workable
name: Prefer later-day return flights
preference_value: Afternoon or evening return departures
rationale: Multiple examples support a recurring preference for later-day return departures. The evidence varies between afternoon, evening, and after 6:00 p.m., so this remains a soft time-of-day default rather than a fixed cutoff.

boundary_condition: Applies only to seat location. If seat selection is unavailable at booking or is deferred until check-in, note that limitation and try to secure a window seat at the earliest available time.
canonical_value: Prefer a window seat by default when selecting a flight seat, while allowing another seat when requested, needed, or no acceptable window seat is available.
condition: When booking or selecting seats for flights where a seat location preference can be applied.
default_action: Prefer or request a window seat by default.
exception_condition: Use a different seat only if the user specifies another seat preference, needs a different seating arrangement, or no acceptable window seat is available.
name: prefers_window_seat_on_flights
preference_value: window seat
rationale: The frozen representative is supported by three explicit examples across separate conversations and expresses a stable default flight seat-location preference with appropriate availability and user-override exceptions.

boundary_condition: Treat the pool and exercise facility as the durable core preference and the hot tub as a softer longitudinal preference. When the current request explicitly says that a pool, hot tub, and fitness center are all required, enforce the complete three-amenity bundle for that search. Do not infer indoor versus outdoor pool requirements, a specific pool type, or unrelated room amenities.

canonical_value.hot_tub: preferred_when_available; required when explicitly stated for the current search

condition: When choosing or comparing hotels based on wellness or recreation amenities.
default_action: Prioritize hotels that offer both a pool and an on-site fitness center, gym, or comparable exercise facility; among otherwise suitable options, prefer one that also has a hot tub.
exception_condition: Relax the hot-tub preference when it materially limits suitable options only if the current request has not made it mandatory. Relax either core amenity when the user explicitly waives it or stronger current-trip constraints favor another hotel; if an explicitly required amenity bundle has no match, confirm with the user before relaxing it.
name: prefers_hotels_with_pool_fitness_and_optional_hot_tub
preference_value: Prefer hotels with both a pool and an on-site fitness facility, with a hot tub as an additional preference when available unless the current search explicitly requires all three amenities.
rationale: These candidates express the same recurring hotel wellness-amenity policy. The pool-and-fitness candidate captures the durable core, while the all-three candidate supplies stronger hot-tub evidence for searches where that amenity is explicitly required. Merging them into the frozen representative preserves a soft longitudinal default without weakening explicit current-trip requirements.

boundary_condition: Treat this as a soft preference because the evidence ranges from tentative interest to a direct requirement.
canonical_value: Prefer hotels with included breakfast.
condition: When evaluating or booking a hotel.
default_action: Prioritize hotels with free breakfast when available, and verify whether breakfast is included if the listing is unclear.
exception_condition: Do not reject an otherwise suitable hotel solely because free breakfast is unavailable unless the user makes it mandatory for the current booking; do not infer requirements about breakfast type or quality.
name: prefer_included_hotel_breakfast
preference_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
rationale: Repeated hotel-selection evidence supports a longitudinal preference for included breakfast. The mixed phrasing warrants retaining the calibrated soft default without strengthening it into a universal requirement.

boundary_condition: Do not infer that the pool or hot tub must be indoor or outdoor; the indoor preference appears in only one dialogue. Do not treat unrelated one-off trip details such as destination, dates, price, or beach proximity as part of this habit.
canonical_value: Prefer hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness or exercise facility.
condition: When choosing or evaluating a hotel for a leisure stay.
default_action: Prioritize or ask about hotels that offer the full pool-plus-hot-tub-plus-fitness/exercise amenity bundle, and call out clearly if one element is missing.
exception_condition: If otherwise suitable hotels do not offer all three amenities, present close matches while explicitly noting which of pool, hot tub, or fitness/exercise facility is absent.
name: hotel_recreation_and_exercise_amenities
preference_value: Prefers hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness/exercise facility.
rationale: Multiple dialogues consistently support a reusable hotel amenity-bundle preference. It is distinct from the breakfast preference, and the supplied fallback appropriately preserves usefulness when no hotel offers the full bundle.

boundary_condition: Carry forward only the general walking-distance preference; do not infer a specific walk-time limit, destination, budget, or rating unless the current request supplies it.
canonical_value: On coastal or beach-oriented trips, prefer lodging on or near the beach or ocean, ideally within walking distance.
condition: When choosing lodging for a coastal or beach-oriented trip.
default_action: Prioritize properties on the beach or close enough to walk, subject to constraints stated for the current trip.
exception_condition: Do not apply this preference to non-coastal trips or when the current request states a different location priority.
name: prefer_beach_proximate_hotels
preference_value: Prefers lodging on or near the beach or ocean, ideally within walking distance.
rationale: These candidates are true aliases supported by the same repeated examples: both express a reusable preference for beach- or ocean-proximate lodging on coastal trips, while treating any exact walk-time, budget, rating, or destination constraint as request-specific.

boundary_condition: Do not infer other amenities, destination, dates, price, views, balcony access, or indoor versus outdoor facility type.
canonical_value: Prefer hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness facility.
condition: When selecting or evaluating hotel options.
default_action: Prioritize hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness or exercise facility, and verify that each is available.
exception_condition: If no suitable property offers all three, ask whether a missing amenity or a reasonable substitute is acceptable.
name: prefer_pool_hot_tub_and_fitness_access
preference_value: Prefers hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness or exercise facility.
rationale: Repeated, well-grounded hotel amenity preference across three conversations; the evidence consistently supports requiring or prioritizing a pool, hot tub, and exercise facility while leaving facility type flexible.

boundary_condition: Do not let free breakfast override explicit trip constraints such as location, price, room setup, or required amenities.
canonical_value: Softly prefer hotels with free breakfast.
condition: When comparing otherwise suitable hotels.
default_action: Rank hotels advertising free breakfast above comparable options that do not include it.
exception_condition: If suitable options do not include free breakfast, present the best matches without treating breakfast as mandatory.
name: prefers_free_breakfast
preference_value: Softly prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
rationale: Free breakfast recurs across three conversations, but wording ranges from tentative to explicit, so retaining it as a soft ranking preference preserves the mixed evidence without overstating it as mandatory.

boundary_condition: Use a 3.5 minimum when the search is explicitly budget-focused. Apply the applicable threshold only to the metric under discussion, and do not conflate hotel class, Google ratings, and customer-review ratings.
canonical_value: Use a soft 4.0 hotel-rating floor for nice, upscale, resort-style, or otherwise well-rated hotel searches, with a 3.5 floor for explicitly budget-focused searches.
condition: When a hotel search calls for a well-rated property, including a nice, upscale, resort-style, or explicitly budget-focused stay, and a rating or hotel-quality metric is available.
default_action: Filter or prioritize options meeting a 4.0 minimum and identify the rating source when known.
exception_condition: Follow any newly stated threshold or metric. If no suitable option meets the applicable floor while satisfying more important trip constraints, ask before relaxing it.
name: contextual_hotel_rating_floor
preference_value: Prefer hotels rated at least 4.0 when seeking a nice, upscale, resort-style, or generally well-rated stay; for explicitly budget-focused searches, prefer at least 3.5.
rationale: The generic 4.0 hotel-quality floor is semantically covered by the calibrated contextual policy's default branch, while the latter also preserves the separately evidenced 3.5 budget fallback and metric distinctions. Keeping both would duplicate the same longitudinal default.

boundary_condition: Apply this only when comparing connecting itineraries; do not infer a general preference for either nonstop flights or flights with a layover.
canonical_value: When evaluating connecting itineraries, prefer at most one short layover that allows a practical transfer and brief break.
condition: When evaluating flight itineraries with connections.
default_action: Prioritize itineraries with at most one layover and a short connection that permits a practical transfer and brief break.
exception_condition: Follow explicit current-trip requirements for a different number or duration of stops.
name: flight_connection_limit_preference
preference_value: When a flight connection is needed, prefer no more than one short layover.
rationale: Repeated evidence supports a soft limit of at most one short layover when a connection is considered, while preserving explicit trip-specific exceptions and avoiding an unsupported general preference between nonstop and connecting flights.

boundary_condition: Treat business class as a soft preference, not a requirement, and do not infer an independent standing budget or price threshold.
canonical_value: Prefer business class when available and feasible; otherwise use coach.
condition: When comparing flight cabin options.
default_action: Prefer or surface business-class options first.
exception_condition: Use coach when business class is unavailable, infeasible under explicit current-trip constraints, or declined by the user.
name: prefer_business_class_with_coach_fallback
preference_value: Prefer business class when available and feasible, with coach acceptable as a fallback.
rationale: The evidence supports business class as a recurring soft cabin preference with coach as the explicit fallback, without establishing a standing budget threshold or making business class mandatory.

boundary_condition: Do not infer preferences for other room amenities, hotel types, destinations, dates, or prices.
canonical_value: Prefer hotel rooms with both an in-room coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge.
condition: When searching for or comparing hotel rooms.
default_action: Use both an in-room coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge as soft amenity criteria.
exception_condition: If otherwise suitable options lack either amenity, confirm whether the preference should be relaxed rather than automatically rejecting them.
name: Prefer an in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge
preference_value: Prefer hotel rooms with both a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge.
rationale: Repeated, consistent evidence supports a durable soft preference for the combination of an in-room coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge. The frozen representative remains unchanged.

boundary_condition: Treat free breakfast as a soft preference; do not infer a required breakfast quality standard.
canonical_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
condition: When searching for or comparing hotels.
default_action: Prefer or surface hotels that include free breakfast.
exception_condition: Relax the preference when the user explicitly deprioritizes breakfast or chooses a hotel without it.
name: Free breakfast hotel preference
preference_value: Prefer hotels with free breakfast.
rationale: Multiple conversations support a recurring preference for free breakfast. Evidence about breakfast quality is mixed and appears only once, so the released policy appropriately retains free breakfast as a soft preference without adding a quality requirement.

boundary_condition: Treat the balcony as a soft amenity preference and do not infer a particular view type; a first-floor room can be acceptable without a balcony.
canonical_value: Softly prefer a hotel room with a balcony, accepting a terrace as a substitute and allowing a first-floor room or an otherwise suitable room without either.
condition: When searching for, selecting, or booking a hotel room
default_action: Prioritize rooms with a balcony when available, confirm availability, and consider a terrace as an acceptable substitute.
exception_condition: Relax the preference when the current request deprioritizes it or suitable balcony or terrace rooms are unavailable, and do not reject an otherwise suitable hotel solely for lacking them.
name: hotel_room_balcony_preference
preference_value: Prefer a hotel room with a balcony; a terrace may be an acceptable substitute.
rationale: Both instances express the same soft hotel-room balcony preference. The second adds terrace as an acceptable substitute, while the frozen representative supplies the first-floor boundary and the general fallback when no balcony is available; these details form one coherent conditional policy without implying a preferred view.

boundary_condition: Apply this per room and do not infer it from the number of travelers or requested rooms.
canonical_value: Prefer a queen-size bed for a shared hotel room when no separate-bed arrangement is requested; accept a king-size bed as a larger alternative.
condition: When selecting a shared hotel room without an explicit request for separate beds.
default_action: Prefer a room with a queen-size bed; a king-size bed may be accepted when offered as a larger alternative.
exception_condition: Honor explicit twin-bed, separate-bed, or other room-specific sleeping arrangements instead.
name: queen_bed_for_shared_hotel_room
preference_value: Prefer a queen-size bed for a shared hotel room when no separate-bed arrangement is requested.
rationale: The frozen representative expresses a reusable, longitudinal room-bed default with explicit boundaries and exceptions. The evidence supports a queen bed as the soft default for a shared room, permits a king as a larger alternative, and preserves explicit separate-bed arrangements.
